why: Artifacts pin the inputs they were computed from. A few of those inputs moved on after the artifact was written and the original bytes no longer exist anywhere, so the pin can never be satisfied again. Recording them here keeps `make verify-pins` meaningful: this inherited drift is acknowledged once, while any NEW drift, or any further change to a file already listed here, still fails the gate. An entry is matched on both path and current hash, so editing one of these files again turns it fatal.
how_to_add: Do not add an entry to make a failing gate pass. An entry is only correct when the pinned bytes are genuinely unrecoverable AND the artifact that pinned them is frozen. If the input still exists somewhere, restore it instead.

known_drift.reason: The phase-1 split manifest was regenerated upstream after the prelaunch audit ran. The audit's own conclusions are frozen and the superseded manifest was never committed, so the pinned bytes are unrecoverable. Inherited from forge; unchanged across every commit in this repository.

A code pin: the preflight artifacts record the hash of the launcher that produced them, and the launcher was edited afterwards. Two artifacts pin two different earlier revisions of the same file, so no single state of it could satisfy both. Inherited from forge; unchanged across every commit in this repository.

Two audits pin two versions of this test file: v1 the earlier one, v2 the current. No single state satisfies both, and the file on disk correctly matches v2, the later audit. Arrived with the f58c679 handoff; not modified in this repository.
